Dynamic path: callers retain resource and realization authority while this crate performs stable-inode locking, descriptor-relative no-follow reads, writes, shredding, exact removal, and atomic no-replace publication; external filesystem durability remains the declared Resource boundary and this is not a direct formal-proof claim.

Static owner: NamespaceSandbox's implementation of the admitted Sandbox contract. Dynamic path: spawn, mount, Artifact access, status, and disposal revalidate the exact root and realization evidence, with destructive cleanup requiring the aggregate-projected effect fence; it creates no parallel Sandbox authority and is not a direct formal-proof claim.

Static owner: the single crash-safe filesystem realization marker shared by Local and Namespace providers. Dynamic path: one locked marker advances create, rebuild, ready, terminal removal, and removed cuts while binding the exact effect fence, immutable fingerprint, physical incarnation, root inode, checkpoint participant, and completion receipt; Session authorization remains upstream and this is not a direct formal-proof claim.

Static owner: physical-incarnation and restore-input identity helpers for the one filesystem realization marker. Dynamic path: creation mints one non-path identity and removed-source recovery accepts only the exact completed checkpoint participant fingerprint, without owning lifecycle state or authorization; this is not a direct formal-proof claim.

Static owner: provider-neutral secret-free completion receipt for Local and Namespace realization. Dynamic path: exact mounts and Memory materializations are validated, sorted, de-duplicated, canonically replayed, and then checked by the provider against its effective spec; this is not a direct formal-proof claim.

Static owner: neutral ACP Session configuration and portable workspace-relative working-directory validation. Dynamic path: publication and Host realization consume this closed value while the selected ACP capability descriptor and Session workspace remain authoritative; this introduces no second capability or filesystem authorization owner and is not a direct formal-proof claim.

Static owner: the sole Session runtime-port projection of one settled Run step, reusing canonical RunState, Pending, Failure, and Run identity instead of defining a second terminal classification. Dynamic path: constructors admit only Awaiting or Ended, terminal event projection is derived from that same state, and Running cannot escape a settled step boundary. The linked absorption obligation covers the canonical Run state machine; message delivery and protocol deduplication remain executable boundary evidence.

The sandbox role owns duplicated pipe/socket descriptors. Actual EOF closes the owned output while reverse traffic drains; protocol framing and domain commands stay in connection-plan and their adapters. This classification covers ownership and cancellation surface, not an OS proof.

FileCatalog owns complete output capture. The canonical reducer validates Workspace/Session identity, nonwrapping revision, unique File ids and exact replay before CAS; transport adapters verify the same receipt. It creates no second artifact store.

Builtin Web provider adapters implement the existing provider port. Direct fetch runs blocking I/O with bounded bodies and disables redirects when a domain filter applies; provider-server tools cannot fall through to host execution. Model routing and authorization remain upstream.

The protocol extension owns output-capture wire DTOs and one GET route; the injected File application owns Workspace authorization and catalog reads. Decimal revision preserves exact browser projection; no output success or acceptance authority is added.

The MCP adapter assembles the Host-selected descriptor/tool set into the existing tool service. A scoped export lease revokes channel peers on shutdown; no permissions or tool state are reconstructed in the transport.

ACP projects messages, ToolBatch, permission ticket and terminal outcome through one ThreadCommit. Only Runtime-owned tickets create a Runtime batch; unconsumed exact permission continuations settle without implying an executed effect was absent.

ACP delegates only uniformly Runtime-owned committed ToolBatches to the existing continuation port. Missing persistence or mixed owners fail closed; recovered Runtime receipts become request context, never another SDK history or acknowledgement store.

The Session Host owns one attached helper and MCP export lease. It revokes admission before TERM/KILL/reap, retains handles across cancellation and leaves final physical disposal to the Session Environment. Bytes do not grant tool authority.

Connection-plan owns bounded byte streams and one yamux driver. Stream drop releases only its capacity and owner drop revokes all streams; no application tool identity, permission or durable replay is interpreted here.

Connection-plan bridges attached stdio and an exact Unix rendezvous with half-close semantics. Socket cleanup compares device/inode before unlink, admission is bounded, and physical owner EOF revokes peers; application state remains above the byte channel.

All three container adapters reuse this immutable-incarnation classifier. Partial identity, multiple objects, fingerprint mismatch or foreign effect fence fail closed; only exact observed absence can report unavailability. Provider observation and durable Session adoption retain separate ownership.

Inbox/Outbox ports and PendingInput moved together from dispatch.rs with their wire tests. Atomic relay-and-enqueue remains one backend transaction; this module split adds no store or formal-proof claim.
